title: Direct-image comparison
statement:
Fix a discrete commutative ring $\Lambda$, using its constant sheaves as coefficients. Let $g\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Base change of site objects gives
the commutative square of topoi

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X_{\Proet}&\xrightarrow{\ \nu_X\ }&X_{\Et}\\
{\scriptstyle g_{\Proet}}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle g_{\Et}}\\
Y_{\Proet}&\xrightarrow{\ \nu_Y\ }&Y_{\Et}
\end{array}
$$

and an isomorphism $g_{\Proet}^*\nu_Y^*\simeq\nu_X^*g_{\Et}^*$ of functors
$\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$, compatible with composition;
since all four functors are exact, it is also an isomorphism of functors
$D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$.

If $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the canonical natural
transformation of functors $D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D^+(Y_{\Proet},\Lambda)$

$$
\nu_Y^*Rg_{\Et,*}K\longrightarrow Rg_{\Proet,*}\nu_X^*K
$$

is an isomorphism for $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. In particular, direct image of
a bounded-below classical pro-étale complex is classical. The isomorphism is
compatible with units, counits and composition.

proof.text: Write $i_T:T_{\Et}\to T_{\Proet}$ for inclusion and $b_g(W)=X\times_Y W$ for either base-change functor. The comparison morphisms and the scheme morphisms of sites are those of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], with the evaluation formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. On every étale object $W/Y$ and every pro-étale sheaf $G$ on $X$, both $\nu_{Y,*}g_{\Proet,*}G$ and $g_{\Et,*}\nu_{X,*}G$ have value $G(X\times_Y W)$, with the same restriction maps. Thus their direct images agree canonically, giving the displayed square of topoi. Its inverse-image identification is precisely the inverse of the isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]; that statement supplies its identity and composition compatibility on sheaves.

proof.text: For any one of the four geometric inverse images $L$, its effect on a constant ring is the canonical constant-ring identification: the constant sheaf functor is left adjoint to global sections (a map out of the sheafified constant presheaf is a compatible family of maps on objects, determined at the terminal object). Hence the composite of $L$ with the source constant-sheaf functor is left adjoint to target global sections, since direct image evaluates at the base-changed terminal object. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies this composite with the target constant-sheaf functor. The identification respects each ring operation. Give $LF$ its scalar endomorphisms by $L(\lambda_a)$ for $a\in\Lambda$; the module identities and linearity of every comparison follow by applying $L$ to their defining equations. Sheafified constant scalars act by gluing these constant actions. This works for every discrete commutative ring, without a finiteness assumption. Exactness on underlying abelian sheaves is [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so forgetting the action detects exactness. All four module inverse images are therefore exact. Since cohomology is a kernel modulo an image, preservation of kernels and cokernels gives $\mathcal H^r(LF^\bullet)\cong L\mathcal H^r(F^\bullet)$; in particular these functors preserve every cohomological lower bound. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to obtain their termwise functors on unbounded derived categories. Apply the sheaf comparison degreewise to complexes and then localize: its inverse, naturality, identity and composition equations remain equations after localization. This proves the first derived assertion.

proof.text:
In the derived categories put $L_1=g_{\Et}^*$, $R_1=Rg_{\Et,*}$, $L_2=g_{\Proet}^*$, $R_2=Rg_{\Proet,*}$, $G=\nu_Y^*$, $H=\nu_X^*$ and let $c:L_2G\xrightarrow{\sim}HL_1$ be step 2. Restrict the input to bounded-below complexes. The exact inverse images preserve this condition by step 2, and $R_1$ preserves it by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Initially regard $R_2H$ in the unbounded target; step 4 identifies it with the bounded-below object $GR_1$ and hence makes the comparison a map in the full bounded-below subcategory. Use the constant-coefficient étale derived adjunction specified in the first paragraph of [sbc-def-base-change-map] (only that general adjunction, with no base-change assertion), with the derived adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] on the pro-étale side. Define the canonical map to be the mate of $c$ in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Explicitly, for $K$ it is
$$G R_1K\xrightarrow{\eta_{2,GR_1K}}R_2L_2GR_1K\xrightarrow{R_2(c_{R_1K})}R_2HL_1R_1K\xrightarrow{R_2H(\varepsilon_{1,K})}R_2HK.$$
Its transpose is $H(\varepsilon_{1,K})\circ c_{R_1K}$, exactly the comparison map specified in the source. All factors are natural in $K$.

proof.text:
Now impose that $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $B=K$, [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives an isomorphism $e:S\xrightarrow{\sim}T$, where $S=GR_1B$ and $T=R_2HB$. We use only this existence assertion, and do not assume e is the mate. By [sk-prop-sf-comparison], both G and H are fully faithful on bounded-below derived categories. For every $A\in D^+(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the following identifications are bijections:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(GA,S)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,R_1B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_1A,B),$$
$$\operatorname{Hom}(GA,T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_2GA,HB)\xrightarrow{c_A}\operatorname{Hom}(HL_1A,HB)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_1A,B).$$
In the second line the c_A identification sends a map v out of L2 GA to $v\circ c_A^{-1}$. Under these identifications, postcomposition with the canonical $\beta_B$ of step 3 is the identity: a map $G(t):GA\to GR_1B$ has transpose
$$H(\varepsilon_{1,B})\circ c_{R_1B}\circ L_2G(t)=H(\varepsilon_{1,B}\circ L_1(t))\circ c_A,$$
by naturality of c, which gives exactly the original adjoint of t. Thus postcomposition with $\beta_B$ is bijective on Hom(GA,-). Take $A=R_1B$, so $GA=S$. Surjectivity supplies $t:S\to S$ with $\beta_Bt=e$. Put $h=te^{-1}:T\to S$. Then $\beta_Bh=1_T$; injectivity applied to $h\beta_B$ and $1_S$ gives $h\beta_B=1_S$. Hence the specified canonical map is invertible, independently of the choice of e. The hypotheses used for e are exactly qcqs g and bounded-below B, with the same discrete coefficients; full faithfulness imposes no properness or constructibility assumption.

proof.text:
Use classicality exactly as defined in the current [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]: for every integer $q$ and every pro-étale affine presentation $U\cong\varprojlim_{i\in I}U_i$, with $I$ small cofiltered and the $U_i$ affine and étale over the base scheme, the restriction map $\varinjlim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}H^q(M)(U_i)	o H^q(M)(U)$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules. Thus a bounded-below classical $M$ lies in $D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ as used by [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence]; this is the same continuity predicate as in the blueprint, not an additional hypothesis. [sk-prop-sf-comparison] supplies the bounded-below derived unit required by that equivalence. Its part 2 therefore gives $K=R
u_{X,*}M\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and a counit isomorphism $
u_X^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. Applying $Rg_{\Proet,*}$ and step 4 identifies $Rg_{\Proet,*}M$ with $
u_Y^*Rg_{\Et,*}K$. Since $Rg_{\Et,*}K$ is bounded below by step 3, part 1 of [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence] for $Y$ makes the latter a bounded-below classical complex. Classicality is invariant under this derived isomorphism: in each degree it gives an isomorphism of cohomology sheaves, whose evaluations and inverses induce inverse maps on the colimits; for a cohomology-sheaf isomorphism $\phi:F\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{\prime}$, naturality of restriction gives $c_{F^{\prime},U}\circ(\varinjlim_i\phi_{U_i})=\phi_U\circ c_{F,U}$. Both $\phi_U$ and $\varinjlim_i\phi_{U_i}$ are invertible, with inverses induced by $\phi^{-1}$. Thus $c_{F^{\prime},U}=\phi_U\circ c_{F,U}\circ(\varinjlim_i\phi_{U_i})^{-1}$. Hence each continuity map for $H^q(Rg_{\Proet,*}M)$ is invertible, for every $q$ and every presentation, as required by [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]. Boundedness is also invariant under this isomorphism, since the cohomology sheaves vanish in the same degrees. The coefficients throughout are the same discrete constant ring $\Lambda$.

proof.text:
Write $\beta:GR_1\to R_2H$ for step 3. Its defining mate formula and its inverse give the two equations
$$\beta_{L_1A}\circ G(\eta_{1,A})=R_2(c_A)\circ\eta_{2,GA},\qquad \varepsilon_{2,HB}\circ L_2(\beta_B)=H(\varepsilon_{1,B})\circ c_{R_1B}.$$
For the first substitute the mate formula and move $G\eta_1$ through $\eta_2$ and $c$ by naturality; the remaining factor is $\varepsilon_1L_1\circ L_1\eta_1=1$. For the second substitute that formula and use $\varepsilon_2L_2\circ L_2\eta_2=1$ after counit naturality. These are exactly compatibility with the units and counits, with their domains displayed. For composable scheme maps, step 2 gives the pasted inverse-image comparison. Apply clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], with the composite adjunctions, to identify its mate with the composite of the two whiskered direct-image comparisons. Clause 4 gives the identity case. This proves composition compatibility for the specified canonical maps, rather than for arbitrarily chosen isomorphisms.
